record.final_answer:
No, there are no published numbers that cover your case.

The only published figure is the Marrowlog 2.4 performance report from 2026 Q2 (https://marrowlog.example/perf/2026-q2). It shows 180,000 lines/s on 1 vCPU at 85% CPU. That sounds like plenty of room above 50k, but the test setup doesn't match yours:

- **No TLS.** Every run used plain TCP. The report says outright that TLS wasn't measured.
- **Short lines.** Every test line was 200 bytes or less. The README says your lines average about 900 bytes, since they're JSON with stack traces.
- **No disk buffer.** It was off in their tests, and it's off in your `config/agent.yaml` as well, so this one doesn't matter for you.

The line length is a bigger worry than it looks. Their result works out to about 36 MB/s (180k × 200 B). Your peak is about 45 MB/s (50k × 900 B). So even over plain TCP, your load is heavier in bytes than anything they measured, and TLS adds encryption cost on top. That's my own rough arithmetic, not a measurement. Cost may not scale linearly with line size, but it means the 180k figure gives you no real headroom.

The maintainers said they'd measure TLS in the Q4 report. I checked and that report isn't out yet (the Q4 page returns 404).

I'd suggest running your own benchmark before you switch: one agent on 1 vCPU, `tls: true`, realistic 900-byte JSON lines and `batch_lines: 500`, run until it hits 50k lines/s. That would give you a real answer well before the end-of-next-quarter deadline, without waiting for Q4.
